trail_brake.coaching: Bleed brake pressure past turn-in — braking shifts weight forward so the front tyres gain grip for rotation.
trail_brake.why: Trail braking uses longitudinal load transfer to increase front normal force while blending into steering (Wikipedia: Trail braking; Driver61 weight-transfer tutorial).

trail_brake_high_downforce.coaching: Trail brake to keep the nose loaded — minimum corner speed builds downforce; release pressure gradually, not in one step.
trail_brake_high_downforce.why: High-downforce cars gain grip with speed; maintaining front load through turn-in preserves rotation without a separate brake release (Track Titan: F1 vs V-line minimum-speed tradeoff).

straight_line_brake.coaching: Brake in a straight line first — separate maximum braking from turn-in so the tyre stays inside the friction circle.
straight_line_brake.why: A tyre has finite combined grip; threshold braking uses full longitudinal capacity before steering loads the contact patch (Sarah Moore Racing: friction circle).

patience_throttle.coaching: Wait until the car points at the exit before full throttle — patience on entry protects exit speed.
patience_throttle.why: Drivers who chase entry speed often destroy exit speed; the lap-time line prioritises the following straight (Driver61 / Mansell late-apex teaching).

early_throttle_vline.coaching: Unwind steering then apply throttle — a straighter exit lets you accelerate earlier on the next straight.
early_throttle_vline.why: The V-line trades mid-corner minimum speed for exit traction; time gained on the straight outweighs the loss (Track Titan V-line guide; LivePhysics GT racing line).

maintenance_throttle.coaching: Light constant throttle through the kink — a lift unloads the tyres and costs grip you cannot see on the map.
maintenance_throttle.why: Fast direction changes need a stable platform; maintenance throttle keeps load on the contact patch through blind or high-speed kinks.
maintenance_throttle.source: Driver61 racing line — fast corner momentum

minimal_steer.coaching: One steering input — sawing at the wheel mid-corner spends grip on corrections instead of acceleration.
minimal_steer.why: The friction circle limits combined brake/steer/throttle; corrections mean you exceeded available grip at that point on the line.

progressive_steer.coaching: Build steering angle smoothly — snap inputs spike lateral demand when the tyre is already loaded.
progressive_steer.why: Progressive steering keeps the combined force vector inside the traction circle through corner entry.
progressive_steer.source: Sarah Moore Racing: friction circle / trail braking

kerb_grip_loss.coaching: Unwind steering when the kerb unloads the tyre — sawing while airborne or on paint wastes grip on recovery.
kerb_grip_loss.why: Stiff suspension and kerb impacts reduce vertical load at the contact patch; F1 teams monitor load-cell spikes for exactly this (Autosport ride quality; Race Sundays kerb vs aero).

kerb_overload.coaching: Clip the kerb, don't launch over it — stay inside travel so the tyre stays in contact with tarmac.
kerb_overload.why: At suspension travel limit the chassis hops and mechanical grip collapses until the tyre reloads (Penske: compliant setup keeps tyres on track).

bump_platform.coaching: Ease inputs over the bump — a vertical hit while braking or turning overloads the tyre instantly.
bump_platform.why: Vertical acceleration spikes transfer through the tyre spring; teams use accelerometers on wheel hubs to separate bump from aero platform control (Autosport F1 setup science).

shift_brake_zone.coaching: Finish downshifts before turn-in — brake in a straight line, blip the throttle to match revs, then rotate.
shift_brake_zone.why: F1 seamless boxes still cut torque on upshifts and apply engine braking on downshifts; drivers sequence shifts in the braking zone with straight steering so the rear stays settled (F1Technical.net transmission guide).

shift_straight_upshift.coaching: Upshift when the wheel is straight — hold the gear through the loaded part of the corner.
shift_straight_upshift.why: Upshifting under lateral load interrupts torque when the tyre needs consistency; straight-line upshifts avoid the mid-corner platform step.
shift_straight_upshift.source: Motorsport Technology — seamless F1 gearbox load transfer
